# Salary calculation reference

This reference documents the **actual formulas used by the website** for its 36
European countries and 11 US cities. Each page combines the model's assumptions
and source notes with exact parameters, executable logic or configuration, and
three representative outputs from the generated dataset.

The modules under [`tools/calc/`](../../tools/calc/) and the US implementation in
[`tools/calc_us.py`](../../tools/calc_us.py) remain the sources of truth. These
pages are generated from them, and CI fails if a formula changes without
regenerating the documentation.

The dated [primary-source audit](audits/2026-10-04-primary-source-audit.md)
separately records which rules have been independently checked, confirmed
discrepancies, and the remaining evidence backlog. Documentation of the current
implementation is not the same as validation of that implementation.

## Keeping calculations current

1. Review every jurisdiction before its new tax year takes effect.
2. Prefer primary tax/social-security authorities; record direct URLs and the
   official worked examples used for validation in the country module docstring.
3. Update the relevant module's tax year, review date, assumptions, constants,
   and formula together.
4. Add or update regression tests for thresholds and authoritative examples.
5. Rebuild data and documentation:

   ```bash
   python3 tools/calc_us.py
   python3 tools/build_formula.py
   python3 tools/generate_calculation_docs.py
   python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
   ```

6. Review the generated documentation diff. Changes to parameters, executable
   code, fingerprints, and representative outputs should all be explainable.

To check for stale generated pages without modifying files:

```bash
python3 tools/generate_calculation_docs.py --check
```

## Scope

The models assume a single employee and the location-specific profile described
on each page. Personal circumstances, regional variation, optional benefits, and
sector-specific charges are generally outside their scope. US city calculations
use the separate [`tools/calc_us.py`](../../tools/calc_us.py) implementation.
